claims: Dynamic-stretching evidence does not make different walking mobility sequences identical.

The candidate is an alternating walk, ipsilateral ankle-or-foot hand hold, comfortable knee-flexion/hip-extension position, release, and step-through; it excludes overhead reach, knee hug, lunge, hop, test, and run.
Warm-up activity sequence matters.
Hand-held ankle/foot, knee flexion, hip extension, and alternating step-through distinguish the base quad-pull contract from knee hugs and overhead-reach sequences.
Acute stretching evidence does not justify isolated-muscle or outcome claims.
The card records knee, hip, stance foot/ankle, pelvis, trunk, shoulder, and elbow task roles without diagnosis or guaranteed tissue change.
Dynamic stretching involves controlled movement.
A valid candidate cycle includes stance, ipsilateral foot/ankle hold, comfortable heel-toward-body knee-flexion position, release, and step-through.
Activity-specific warm-up conditions differ.
Scores describe exercise coordination and physical demand only, never athlete proficiency or age.
Acute effects depend on type, dose, timing, and surrounding activity.
Track sides, cycles, range, hand hold, pace, support, symptoms, and downstream work; no universal recovery claim is made.
Instruction, supervision, environment, and progressive exposure are relevant safeguards.
Use a clear lane, controlled pace, optional stable support, communication, and exit without demographic classification.
Dose varies across dynamic-stretching protocols.
Candidate cycle and range proposals remain review-only and stop before forced range, lumbar compensation, or balance loss.
Implementation matters to the activity that follows.
Cue a controlled walk, light ankle/foot hold, comfortable heel-toward-body position, release, and step-through without promising flexibility or performance transfer.
Safe training requires appropriate instruction and environment.
Stop for pain, neurologic/circulatory symptoms, dizziness, unsafe balance or lane, inability to communicate, or a stop request.
Interpret acute stretching with dose and subsequent dynamic activity in view.
Select only after session inputs, logistics, duration, fatigue, substitutions, and downstream demands are validated.
A single dynamic movement is not a guaranteed intervention.
Use plain range, balance, breathing, and stop checks; a support option or other reviewed task may be appropriate.
Warm-up components are context-dependent.
Observe side sequence, ankle/foot hold, knee/hip action, trunk/pelvis compensation, range, pace, and symptoms without diagnosing restriction.
Instruction and safe environments are implementation safeguards.
Captions, transcript, still sequence, lane markers, support, and verbal cueing remain candidate supports; media accessibility is not assumed.
Dynamic-movement categories do not establish mechanical equivalence.
The alternate review separates overhead reach, stationary support, knee hug, lunge, test intent, pace, and range from the base quad-pull contract.
Task-specific instruction remains a safeguard.
Two oEmbed titles name the base task and one names overhead reach; all remain candidate-only pending full human media review.

assessmentSummary.identity: One Walking Quad Pull cycle is a controlled forward step, single-leg stance, ipsilateral hand hold of the ankle or foot, comfortable heel-toward-body knee-flexion and hip-extension position without forced lumbar extension, release, and step-through to the other side. It is not Walking Quad Pull with Overhead Reach, Walking Knee Hug, a stationary quad stretch, lunge, hop, balance assessment, or run.
currentCardFindings: Source 51 omits a cycle boundary, hand hold, range, support, lane, fatigue, substitution, and review contract.
Overhead reach is a changed action sequence and remains a separate card.
Two direct-title and one overhead-reach oEmbed candidates are recorded without exact-match or approval claims.

calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No universal range, dose, recovery, readiness, outcome, or score is established; human review remains required.
